title.narrative: Partnering with SIDS to deliver a 75% reduction in Plastic Pollution

description.narrative: Partner countries: Grenada, St Lucia, Papua New Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Tuvalu. Regional components include the Pacific, Caribbean, and Indian Ocean regions.

Partnering with SIDS to build sustainable blue economies through reduction in plastic pollution.
This programme supports Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to reduce plastic pollution through evidence-based national policy plans, implementation-readiness support, and complementary regional solutions.
During Phase I (2024–2025), Common Seas supported partner countries to develop five national policy plans and recommendation reports across Grenada, Saint Lucia, Papua New Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, and Tuvalu. These outputs established plastic waste baselines, modelled future pollution scenarios, and identified policy pathways with the potential to reduce plastic pollution by approximately 40% to 79% over ten years.
During the extension phase (2025–2026), the programme moved from policy development into implementation readiness. This included financial assessments for Saint Lucia and Guinea-Bissau, embedded technical support to strengthen institutional capacity, and development of a Scope of Work for a regional Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) feasibility study with the Indian Ocean Commission.
Phase III (April 2026 – March 2027), running from April 2026 to March 2027, will continue this phased approach. It will support selected countries to advance implementation readiness and early delivery, including implementation finance in Papua New Guinea, institutional capacity support in Grenada or Tuvalu, a reuse-focused pilot in Saint Lucia, follow-on feasibility work for regional EPR in the Indian Ocean, and structured engagement with private sector actors.
The programme combines country-level support with regional collaboration to help SIDS move from policy frameworks toward finance-ready and implementable solutions, while supporting long-term reductions in plastic pollution and associated greenhouse gas emissions.

Small Island Developing States (SIDS), including national government institutions, regional organisations, local delivery partners, civil society, and private sector stakeholders involved in plastic pollution reduction, waste management, circular economy solutions, and sustainable blue economy development.
